definition: Learning a distance function or embedding space where similar items are close — the machinery behind face recognition and retrieval.
details: Learning a distance function or embedding space where similar items are close — the machinery behind face recognition and retrieval.

explainer.lead: Metric learning learns a distance function or embedding space where similar items are close together. It matters because that embedding machinery powers face recognition and retrieval.

tiers.eli5: It teaches a computer a sense of closeness, so photos of the same person land near each other and different people land far apart. Then finding a match is just looking for the nearest neighbour.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train embeddings so that distances reflect similarity, then use nearest-neighbour search for recognition and retrieval. The pitfall is that the learned distance reflects the training data's notion of similarity, which may not match the deployment setting.
tiers.paperLevel: Learning a distance function or embedding space in which similar items are close; the machinery behind face recognition and retrieval. Its behaviour is bounded by the similarity structure present in the training data.

explainer.example: A face-recognition system embeds each face so that two images of the same person are close and images of different people are far apart.
